summary: Snowy Mountain tower, Hamilton County NY: 22-ft steel Aermotor tower built 1917, extended 1933, in operation until 1971, restored and NRHP-listed 2001; open to the public.

facts.design: 22-foot prefabricated Aermotor LS40 steel tower built 1917, extended by 20 feet in 1933

access.note: Wikipedia says it has been restored and is open to the public. The trail is in the Jessup River Wild Forest and is reached from State Route 30 (FFLA April 2024).

visit.trail_note: A hike, not a drive-up. The FFLA newsletter says the 2024 repair day would require a long hike. The trail is popular and has suffered from overuse. The sources read do not say whether the cab is open to climbers now; check with NYSDEC before climbing.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Lookout established atop a 15-foot tower at a cost of $989.02, before the 1917 steel tower
22-foot steel tower erected; prefabricated Aermotor LS40 design
20-foot extension added so the cab sees over the trees (NHLR); four more flights of stairs added (Wikipedia)
In operation until 1971 (NHLR); closed in 1971 as aerial detection arrived (Wikipedia)
Added to the National Register of Historic Places, September 23, 2001
Restored by DEC staff, Student Conservation Corps and local citizens, with NYS Police helicopter support
FFLA report (dated January 19, 2005) lists Snowy among Adirondack towers already restored
Safety-fencing repair work announced for July 13 and 14, 2024; completion not confirmed

corrections.why: The Register describes a 22-foot tower with a 20-foot extension added in 1933, about 42 feet (12.8 m). Wikipedia gives 45 feet (14 m). No source read supports 4.6 m.

corrections.current: Restored in 2011 by Forest Ranger Greg George with many partners
corrections.proposed: Restored in 2001 by DEC staff, Student Conservation Corps and local citizens
corrections.why: The Register gives 2001, and the FFLA January 2005 report already lists Snowy as restored. The 2011 date comes from andyarthur.org, which returned HTTP 403 and could not be read.

corrections.current: Volunteers attached new safety fencing to the tower on a July work day
corrections.proposed: Safety-fencing repair work planned for July 13 and 14, 2024; completion not confirmed
corrections.why: The April 2024 newsletter describes the July work as planned, not as done.

notes_for_editor: The brief's andyarthur.org page for Snowy returned HTTP 403 and was not readable. Its claims of a 1923 observer's cabin, a 2011 restoration led by Greg George, and the July 2024 fencing being completed are therefore unverified. The 1923 cabin is not in facts or events. The 2011 and 2024 items are corrected above because NHLR, the 2005 FFLA report and the April 2024 newsletter conflict with them. The NRHP nomination PDF is not digitized per NPGallery, so only its record metadata was used. Height is unresolved: NHLR implies about 42 ft, Wikipedia says 45 ft; 12.8 m is used with the conflict recorded. NHLR's photo (courtesy Laurie Rankin, Feb 2018) was not added because no image URL was found. The 2004 FFLA report lists the restored towers in prose and does not state a date for Snowy's restoration.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives a 22-foot tower plus a 20-foot extension (about 42 feet, 12.8 m). Wikipedia gives 45 feet (14 m). The facts use the Register figure and the story notes the difference.
The Register gives 2001 and Wikipedia gives no date. The brief's 2011 date rests on a page that could not be read. The FFLA 2005 report already lists Snowy as restored, which fits 2001.
